difficulty_reason: The target recovers every thin quotient in a nested standard-table-algebra chain from a degree formula, through a new double-coset degree-constancy criterion and recursive quotient-chain reconstruction. Even after the named quotient and homomorphism prerequisites, the bidirectional induction and exact multiplicative transfer remain substantive proof obligations beyond routine qualification-exam arguments. No later integrality or nilpotence result contributes to this rating.
source_scope_note: Prove exactly Theorem1.7: for a finite-dimensional complex standard table algebra and a strictly nested bi-anchored chain, thinness is equivalent to the printed degree/product-of-successive-double-coset-cardinalities formula for every1<=i<=n and b in C_(i-1) minus C_i. One bidirectional criterion is selected. The complete new chain-factorization and both degree-constancy quotient inductions are included. Later divisibility, p-standard, nilpotence, and counterexample assertions are preserved as uncounted author context. Frobenius--Perron degree-map foundations, standard table-algebra quotient/homomorphism theory and the closed-subset correspondence are explicitly cited original prerequisites. Lemma3.3 and Theorem3.4 and both thinness implications remain new core, never granted. The exact author proof retains its literal i=0 phrases at952/956/958, while the selected original statement and definition of m at294--307 use1<=i<=n. No bound or C_(i-1) edit is supplied. The vacuous b in B minus C_0 language in the supporting criterion is preserved. Root source decision remains separate.
